{"marker":"EVAL_MIGRATION","sql":"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;

BEGIN IMMEDIATE;

DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_contacts_tenant_normemail;

-- Treat only NULL and all-space emails as missing identities.
UPDATE contacts
SET email = NULL
WHERE email IS NOT NULL
  AND email <> ''
  AND trim(email) = '';

-- Normalize retained nonmissing emails. Empty string is a valid identity.
UPDATE contacts
SET email = lower(trim(email))
WHERE email IS NOT NULL
  AND (email = '' OR lower(trim(email)) <> '')
  AND email <> lower(trim(email));

-- Repoint tickets from duplicate losers to winners before deleting losers.
WITH ranked AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT id,
         tenant_id,
         lower(trim(email)) AS canonical_email,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY tenant_id, lower(trim(email))
           ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC
         ) AS rn
  FROM contacts
  WHERE email IS NOT NULL
    AND (email = '' OR lower(trim(email)) <> '')
),
mapping AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT loser.id AS loser_id,
         winner.id AS winner_id
  FROM ranked AS loser
  JOIN ranked AS winner
    ON winner.rn = 1
   AND loser.rn > 1
   AND loser.tenant_id = winner.tenant_id
   AND loser.canonical_email = winner.canonical_email
)
UPDATE tickets
SET contact_id = (
  SELECT mapping.winner_id
  FROM mapping
  WHERE mapping.loser_id = tickets.contact_id
)
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM mapping
  WHERE mapping.loser_id = tickets.contact_id
);

-- Delete losing duplicate contacts only after ticket repointing.
WITH ranked AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT id,
         tenant_id,
         lower(trim(email)) AS canonical_email,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY tenant_id, lower(trim(email))
           ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC
         ) AS rn
  FROM contacts
  WHERE email IS NOT NULL
    AND (email = '' OR lower(trim(email)) <> '')
)
DELETE FROM contacts
WHERE id IN (
  SELECT id
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rn > 1
);

-- Future normalized uniqueness: same identity, nonmissing only, per tenant.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_contacts_tenant_normemail
ON contacts(tenant_id, lower(trim(email)))
WHERE email = '' OR (email IS NOT NULL AND lower(trim(email)) <> '');

COMMIT;
","rationale":"Single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with foreign_keys=ON before writes. Missing identities are exactly NULL or all-space, normalized to NULL and excluded from dedupe/index. A partial unique expression index enforces tenant_id + lower(trim(email)) only for nonmissing identities. Drop/recreate index inside the transaction is idempotent and rollbackable; no triggers, table rebuilds, or FK disabling."}

FROM contacts AS c
JOIN (
    SELECT id,
           tenant_id,
           email,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY tenant_id, email
               ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC
           ) AS rn
      FROM contacts
     WHERE email IS NOT NULL
) AS w
  ON w.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
 AND w.email = c.email
 AND w.rn = 1
 AND w.id <> c.id
WHERE c.email IS NOT NULL;

-- 4. Repoint tickets to winners before deleting losers.
UPDATE tickets
   SET contact_id = (
           SELECT m.winner_id
             FROM temp.migration_loser_winner AS m
            WHERE m.loser_id = tickets.contact_id
       )
 WHERE tickets.contact_id IN (
           SELECT loser_id
             FROM temp.migration_loser_winner
       );

-- 5. Delete only losing duplicate contacts.
DELETE FROM contacts
 WHERE id IN (
       SELECT loser_id
         FROM temp.migration_loser_winner
       );

-- 6. Enforce future nonmissing normalized uniqueness per tenant.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_contacts_tenant_normemail
    ON contacts(tenant_id, lower(trim(email)))
 WHERE email IS NOT NULL
   AND trim(email) <> '';

COMMIT;","rationale":"Uses one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction after setting foreign_keys=ON and busy_timeout outside the transaction. Normalizes missing emails to NULL without merging them, normalizes nonmissing emails to lower(trim(email)), then builds a loser->winner map with ROW_NUMBER ordered by updated_at DESC, id DESC. Tickets are repointed to winners before losers are deleted, so foreign keys are never disabled and child references remain valid. The partial unique expression index IF NOT EXISTS enforces the same normalized nonmissing uniqueness per tenant while excluding missing emails; all DDL/DML is transactional and a runner that stops on first error and issues ROLLBACK can rollback atomically."}
cases.goal:
Deliver a production SQLite 3.45+ migration script for this legacy help-desk database.
Existing schema, with foreign_keys=ON:
CREATE TABLE contacts(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  email TEXT, display_name TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE tickets(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, contact_id INTEGER NOT NULL
  REFERENCES contacts(id), subject TEXT NOT NULL);
Legacy contacts may duplicate an email within one tenant. Identity is tenant_id plus
lower(trim(email)), where trim removes ordinary ASCII spaces. Missing means email IS NULL or
trim(email)='': this includes empty strings and all-space strings. Preserve each missing
contact separately and normalize its email to NULL.
For each nonmissing duplicate identity, keep the row with greatest updated_at, breaking
ties by greatest id. Preserve that winner's id, display_name, tenant_id and updated_at.
Repoint every ticket to the winning contact before deleting losers. Preserve all ticket
IDs and subjects. Normalize retained nonmissing emails. Enforce this same normalized
uniqueness rule for FUTURE INSERTs and UPDATEs, without merging across tenants or making
missing emails unique. Add a unique index, without triggers or rebuilding the tables.
Never disable foreign-key enforcement.
The script must be atomic, including creation of the uniqueness constraint. If a statement
fails before COMMIT the transaction must still be rollbackable. Running the script twice
must produce the same data and constraints. Do not assume a particular row count or IDs.
Organize the work in dependent stages: have independent agents analyze data/FK invariants
and transaction/retry hazards; use their findings for an implementation agent; then have
a separate agent inspect that candidate for concrete counterexamples before delivery.
Correct any issue they identify within this run. You do not have a SQL execution tool,
so do not claim execution; deliver the script for an external SQLite evaluator.
Return ONLY JSON: {"marker":"EVAL_MIGRATION","sql":"complete script", "rationale":"..."}.
